newsitem.title: USA: US CREDIT MARKET OUTLOOK - Prices seen range bound.
newsitem.headline: US CREDIT MARKET OUTLOOK - Prices seen range bound.

text.p: Little price movement was expected in the U.S. bond market Tuesday as participants had a light slate of economic data to trade on and awaited more comprehensive readings on the labor market.

Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan has stated that he would look to signs of wage inflation as a trigger to tighten monetary policy further. The Fed increased short-term interest rates by 25 basis points at its last policy-making meeting on March 25. The FOMC next meets on May 20 and market participants believed further tightening was likely.

The Treasury was scheduled to sell $17 billion of two-year notes Tuesday and $12.5 billion of five-year notes on Wednesday. In when-issued trade late on Monday, two-year notes were yielding 6.460 percent and the five-year notes were yielding 6.7255 percent.

David Levy, director of forecasting at the Jerome Levy Economics Institute at Bard College, said economic growth in the first quarter obviously had been strong due to an extremely mild winter in many parts of the country.
Three added days of construction work in a month made a huge impact, Levy said.
Levy said much of the concern the Fed has expressed about stock market valuations may lead it to be make another tightening move.

"I'd call this our noodling phase," said Hugh Johnson, economist at First Albany Corp. He expected yields on the Treasury's long bond to remain in a range of 7.0 percent to 7.15 percent until definitive signs the economy was slowing surfaced.

Johnson said the odds of a further tightening may be lessening as initial unemployment claims, industrial materials and the price of gold were falling. Auto sales and nonfarm payrolls were the next critical data, he said.

"I'm a long way from convinced that the Fed will raise rates," Johnson said. He looked forward to the Labor Department's Employment Cost Index on April 29 as the next key economic indicator. Johnson said the Fed likely would focus on the benefits component of the index as a harbinger of future inflationary pressure.
Following that will be the National Association of Purchasing Management's reading on manufacturing activity and the nonfarm payrolls report, he said.
The Fed hiked short-term interest rates at its last meeting om March 25.
Celeste Summerville, senior analyst at GovPX, noted that trading volume had been headed toward record lows for recent trends and was closing about 16 percent below recent levels.
"There was no pickup from the two- and five-year when-issued trade. For some reason or another we did pickup in volume" late in the afternoon," said Summerville.
"There's a possibility things could remain light. There's not really much on the calendar the rest of the week," Summerville said.
The 30-year bond was trading down 14/32 at 94-08 to yield 7.09 percent late Monday.

At the short end of the maturity spectrum three-month bills were two basis points lower at 5.13 percent; six-month bills were unchanged at 5.40 percent and ayear bills were up three basis points at 5.62 percent.
Two-year notes down 2/32 at 99-22/32 to yield 6.42 percent. Five-year notes were 5/32 lower at 99-15/32 to yield 6.75 percent and 10-year issues were 9/32 lower at 95-20/32 to yield 6.87 percent.
